rationale:
OWNER RULING 2026-08-24, D2 of bugs_closed/305: "correct that instruction narrowly".

WHAT IT IS. ai-agent-orchestration.com's brief mandates a canonical tagline - 'Multi-agent systems deployed to production in days, not months - on Kubernetes, Kafka, and Postgres' - and orders it into six placements (footer on all pages, homepage hero, services hero, about page, meta descriptions, page-level hero subheadlines). The mandated sentence is itself a define-by-negation, which is the exact construction the owner objected to in 305, so the site was instructed to make that construction its signature line. This migration removes ONLY the negation clause: 'in days, not months' -> 'in days'. The stack-specificity is the strong half and is carried verbatim.

WHY CODE COULD NOT FIX IT. The copy gate EXEMPTS a phrase the brief supplied - designed in over four council rounds, and correct: the writer was ORDERED to use this sentence, so repairing it would mean the system silently disobeying its own brief. This is the one instance in 305 the gate can never fix by itself, which is precisely why it was escalated to the owner as D2.

FIVE COPIES, NOT ONE, AND HALF A FIX IS INDISTINGUISHABLE FROM NO FIX. [MEASURED 2026-08-24] The sentence is duplicated across three aspects and five keys: content_direction.emphasis, content_direction.formatted, identity.core_value_proposition, site_plan.strategy_notes, and site_plan.content_direction. The gate's exemption is computed over the FLATTENED brief corpus (679 strings across all aspects on this site), so while ANY copy retains the old phrase the exemption keeps firing and no page changes. Correcting identity alone - which is what every prior doc in this lane said to do - would have achieved nothing observable.

THE NESTED-SPEC TRAP, and why the obvious patch is wrong. site_plan.content_direction is an OBJECT (3598 chars), not a string. The natural edit - jsonb_set(data,'{k}',to_jsonb(replace(data->>'k',...))) - FLATTENS it to a JSON string and destroys the spec. This migration replaces at the DOCUMENT level (data::text -> replace -> ::jsonb), which is structure-preserving for both shapes and is safe here specifically because neither needle nor replacement contains a quote, backslash or brace, so the serialised JSON stays valid and only string CONTENTS change. A post-condition asserts jsonb_typeof(...) = 'object' so a future 'simplification' back to the naive form fails loudly; that assertion was INDUCED (flattened the object by hand in a rolled-back transaction; it raised).

A SEPARATE TRAP WORTH RECORDING: the tagline is NOT in the columns called tagline. sites.tagline and site_specs.identity->>'tagline' both hold 'Production-Grade Multi-Agent Systems. Built Right.' - a different sentence, untouched here and verified untouched after apply. Anyone told to 'fix the tagline' edits those and changes the wrong line. Found by following the LANDMINES entry for identity-sourced fields, which prescribes putting the stores side by side before proposing any fix.

DEMAND CONTROL, run after apply with the shipped scanner over real content_data and the corrected 679-string brief: adoption-tracker's hero sentence now reports REPAIRABLE where it previously reported exempt:brief_supplied_sentence. So correcting the instruction automatically un-exempts the existing copy, and the gate repairs it on the next ordinary render - no page editing by hand, and none should be attempted.

Versioned rather than overwritten (the 585 pattern): supersede + re-insert, so the brief's history survives - 11 superseded rows still carry the original sentence.

plan.summary: Remove the define-by-negation clause from ai-agent-orchestration.com's mandated canonical tagline, across all five brief locations that carry it, versioned rather than overwritten. Config-only, live on apply.

edits.rationale: One CTE supersedes every current spec row carrying the phrase and re-inserts a corrected copy in the same statement, so there is no window with two current rows and no window with none. Document-level replace preserves the nested object that a key-level jsonb_set would flatten. Needle-gated on the phrase, so a re-run is a no-op.
edits.sketch:
WITH superseded AS (
  UPDATE site_specs ss SET is_current=false, superseded_at=now() FROM sites s
   WHERE s.id=ss.site_id AND s.domain='ai-agent-orchestration.com' AND ss.is_current
     AND ss.data::text LIKE '%in days, not months%'
  RETURNING ss.site_id, ss.aspect, ss.data, ss.source, ss.source_agent, ss.source_item_id, ss.pinned)
INSERT INTO site_specs (site_id, aspect, data, source, source_agent, source_item_id, pinned, notes, is_current, created_at, created_by)
SELECT site_id, aspect, replace(data::text,'in days, not months','in days')::jsonb, source, source_agent, source_item_id, pinned, '<note>', true, now(), 'migration-597-d2-tagline' FROM superseded;

edits.rationale: Precheck aborts unless exactly 3 current rows carry the phrase, so a brief that has moved on since this was written stops rather than being half-edited. Post-conditions assert: zero current rows retain the old phrase (a partial correction leaves the exemption armed and changes nothing); exactly 3 carry the corrected sentence; and site_plan.content_direction is STILL an object. Both the zero-remaining and the object assertions were INDUCED before applying and both raised.
edits.sketch:
IF old_left <> 0 THEN RAISE EXCEPTION '597 FAILED: % current spec row(s) still carry the old phrase', old_left; END IF;
IF obj_ok <> 1 THEN RAISE EXCEPTION '597 FAILED: site_plan.content_direction is no longer an object'; END IF;

edits.rationale: Restores by re-activating the superseded rows rather than editing text back, so the pre-597 bytes are exactly what returns. Its banner states that reverting re-mandates the sentence the owner objected to and re-arms the exemption, and that this is a CONTENT decision needing the owner rather than a session.
edits.sketch:
UPDATE site_specs SET is_current=false, superseded_at=now() ... WHERE notes LIKE '%Migration 597.%';
UPDATE site_specs SET is_current=true, superseded_at=NULL ... WHERE NOT is_current AND data::text LIKE '%in days, not months%';

grounded_in: The instruction being changed, verbatim from site_specs identity.core_value_proposition: 'Multi-agent systems deployed to production in days, not months - on Kubernetes, Kafka, and Postgres. This should be the canonical tagline used consistently in: site footer across all pages, homepage hero section, services page hero, about page, meta descriptions where appropriate, and any page-level hero subheadlines.'

The five locations, with types, measured 2026-08-24: content_direction.emphasis (string), content_direction.formatted (string), identity.core_value_proposition (string), site_plan.strategy_notes (string), site_plan.content_direction (OBJECT, 3598 chars).
Why partial does not work: the gate's exemption is computed over the flattened brief corpus - 679 strings across all current aspects on this site, counted by the shipped canary.
Demand control after apply, shipped scanner over real page_components.content_data: adoption-tracker's hero returns REPAIRABLE where the pre-597 run returned exempt:brief_supplied_sentence.

Post-apply controls: zero current spec rows retain the old phrase; 11 superseded rows preserve it; sites.tagline still reads 'Production-Grade Multi-Agent Systems. Built Right.' (a different sentence, deliberately untouched).

The LANDMINES entry for identity-sourced fields, whose prescribed check ('put the three stores side by side and read the row') is what revealed that the columns named tagline hold a different sentence entirely.
Owner ruling, 2026-08-24, in response to a written explanation of D2: 'D2 correct that instruction narrowly.'
plan.risks:
THE PAGES DO NOT CHANGE UNTIL THEY RE-RENDER. 7 components across 5 pages still carry the old sentence in stored content_data; they become ordinary repairable hits rather than exempt ones, and the gate fixes them on the next render. Nothing should be hand-edited - that is what 305 spent four council rounds avoiding.

A RE-RENDER OF THIS SITE IS CURRENTLY BLOCKED for reasons unrelated to this change: 30+ open needs_human_review items including claims_unverified on protocol-tracker. So the visible effect is deferred, and a session measuring the pages tomorrow will still see the old sentence. That is expected, not a failed migration - measure the SPEC, not the page, to check this landed.

WIDER BLAST RADIUS THAN THE ONE SENTENCE, stated plainly: replacing at document level touches every occurrence of the needle in three whole spec documents. Measured, that is exactly the five known occurrences and nothing else, because the needle is a distinctive six-word phrase. A shorter needle would not have been safe this way.

NOT ADDRESSED HERE: content_direction separately carries define-by-negation in nine other keys - the general half of D2, and a larger content decision than the owner's narrow ruling covers. Deliberately out of scope. Eight other site briefs across the estate carry the same shape and are each their own lane's call.
